static_traits.name: Li Bowen
static_traits.social_status: Strained relationships with colleagues (due to self-doubt about one's teaching ability)
static_traits.medical_history: No experience of similar problems; no previous psychotherapy; no significant physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to concretely describe their own thoughts and feelings; attitude is rather negative (self-doubt); cooperative and willing to try behavioral experiments; overgeneralization and personalization cognitions often appear; speech rate and thinking logic not mentioned

basic_info.main_problem: Because a high school student got an F, I feel I am a bad teacher; this belief has led to increased stress and feelings of inadequacy.
basic_info.core_demands: These feelings of self-inadequacy are affecting my teaching performance and causing marked distress, so I decided to seek counseling.

special_situations.event: First noticing the student's F grade (about a month ago)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my student fails, it means my teaching ability is poor
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Improves teaching methods and gives the student extra attention
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This must be my fault; I am a bad teacher.

special_situations.event: Each time in class or when seeing that student
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot get every student to meet the standard, it proves my teaching is incompetent overall
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly reflects on and adjusts own teaching in the classroom, trying to correct problems with higher standards
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If one student fails, then my teaching for all students is no good.

special_situations.event: When receiving praise from parents or seeing other students perform well
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Positive feedback does not matter; as long as one student fails, it shows I am incompetent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignoring positive evidence, focusing attention on that student's failure
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: These good reviews do not count; I am still a bad teacher.

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized as a competent teacher, hoping to help every student achieve passing grades
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being seen as incompetent, fearing disappointing students and suffering others' evaluation
defense_goal: Maintaining a sense of control over teaching outcomes by attributing failure to oneself
Avoiding being seen as incompetent again by raising standards and redoubling effort

object_relations.self_representation: A failing and guilty teacher (feels 'I am letting him and myself down')

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor guides them to focus on positive evidence or proposes behavioral experiments to seek a more balanced perspective
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tends to think positive evidence 'does not count', continuing to regard students' failures as decisive evidence of their own incompetence
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Self-blaming tone, repeatedly emphasizing 'it is all my fault', weakening or negating positive feedback; the counselor uses gentle, concretizing, and quantifying questions to gradually guide them to identify and loosen the self-blame pattern.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked whether there is evidence contradicting the 'bad teacher' belief (such as other students' good performance and parents' praise)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Treats positive evidence as 'exceptions' insufficient to change the conclusion, finding seemingly plausible reasons for self-negation
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizes the 'decisiveness' of negative evidence in a gentle tone, while downplaying positive information; the counselor can use rhetorical questions and summaries to help them distinguish facts from inferences.

manifestations: When communicating with spouse, receives support but feels 'not quite understood'
Feeling trapped in class or when seeing that student

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequent self-doubt and attributing students' failure to oneself
Still persistently negating oneself when facing positive feedback

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Taking 'teachers must be fully responsible for student grades' as an absolute standard
Equates an individual student's failure with one's own incompetence

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'.
manifestations: When parents' praise or other students' good performance is mentioned, immediately turns to emphasizing the F grades, avoiding contact with positive experiences

exception_events.target_problem: When seeing that student or teaching class, the client usually experiences strong self-negation and stress, and believes they are an incompetent teacher, which in turn affects classroom performance and sleep.
exception_events.unique_outcome: When communicating with a spouse, receiving listening and support.
exception_events.reason: Different support: spouse's support and listening provided emotional support.

exception_events.target_problem: When facing students' F grades, the client usually ignores other evidence and persistently believes their teaching ability is poor.
exception_events.unique_outcome: On some occasions, parents gave positive praise and other students performed well, providing positive evidence for their teaching effectiveness.
exception_events.reason: Different evidence and external positive feedback: praise from parents and the good performance of other students become counter-narrative clues.

positive_force: Proactively seeks professional help and is willing to try behavioral experiments
Some students perform well; parents have given positive feedback
Has proactively improved teaching and given the student extra attention
negative_force: A cognitive pattern of overgeneralization and personalization
Tending to ignore positive evidence, persistent self-negation
Repeated self-scrutiny leads to strained relationships with colleagues

target_behavior.behavior: Strong self-blame and anxiety when seeing the student or teaching class
antecedent: Thinking about one's own teaching performance
target_behavior.core_reason: Overgeneralizes the failure of individual students into a sense of being wholly incompetent, and takes full responsibility in a personalized way
target_behavior.function: Maintains a sense of control over outcomes and prompts self-improvement through self-reproach, while avoiding uncertain external factors
target_behavior.consequence: Teaching performance is affected, relationships with colleagues are strained, stress increases and affects sleep and overall health
